original_description: Keep performance from regressing as agents ship changes - adopt perf-policy.toml (benchmarks, noise-calibrated tolerances, budgets for latency, startup, memory, bundle size, query/exec counts and Core Web Vitals) on top of test-skills' R1-R5 rigor tiers, and wire a CI gate that builds base and head on the same runner, compares them interleaved and paired with a confidence-interval rule (perfkit suite + gate), reads its policy from the base branch so a PR can't loosen it, and is proven to fail on an injected regression and pass a clean change; CodSpeed, Bencher, github-action-benchmark, Lighthouse CI and size-limit where they fit. Use this skill whenever the user asks to add performance or benchmark checks to CI, catch perf regressions in PRs, set performance budgets or SLOs, track benchmarks over time, fix flaky perf tests, gate bundle size or Lighthouse scores, or add performance rules for agents to a repo. For one-off measurement use perf-measure; for optimizing use perf-optimize.

final_description: Use this skill when someone wants performance protected automatically going forward, not measured or improved once. Reach for it whenever the request is about making CI or code review enforce performance: failing or blocking PRs that make the app slower, heavier, or more resource-hungry; setting budgets, thresholds or SLOs (bundle size, startup, latency, memory, Web Vitals); adding Lighthouse CI, size-limit, CodSpeed or Bencher; tracking benchmark results over time with alerts on regressions, on any CI system (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, etc.); making flaky perf checks reliable; or writing rules so AI agents must show performance didn't regress before merging. Includes calibrating tolerances and proving the gate catches a real regression. Not for one-off profiling or verifying a speedup claim (perf-measure), nor for actually making code faster or smaller (perf-optimize).

history.description: Use this skill when the goal is to stop performance from getting worse over time in a repo: automated, enforced checks that run on every pull request or merge. Typical asks: make PRs fail if they slow the app down or make it bigger; set budgets or thresholds for bundle size, startup time, latency, memory or Core Web Vitals; add Lighthouse CI, size-limit, CodSpeed or Bencher; build a perf gate that compares base and head on the same runner and fails only on statistically real regressions; track benchmarks over time and alert on drift; fix flaky perf checks; or write rules that require agents to prove performance before merging. Covers the policy file, noise-calibrated tolerances, CI wiring and proving the gate fails on a real regression. Not for one-off profiling or measuring (use perf-measure) or for making code faster (use perf-optimize).
